extracted.subtask_description: Advice and categorical examples for crafting the first line(s) of a book or novel to hook readers; includes tone categories and practical tips for writing memorable openings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mysterious and intriguing
rubrics_metrics.description: A category of opening lines that generate curiosity by presenting something puzzling, eerie, or unexplained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hints or strange details that raise questions and invite the reader to keep reading to find answers; set an enigmatic tone rather than explaining everything up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorous and witty
rubrics_metrics.description: A category of openings that rely on humor, clever phrasing, or a witty voice to engage the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a punchy, unexpected observation or comic turn of phrase that establishes tone and voice while demonstrating the book's wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmospheric and descriptive
rubrics_metrics.description: A category of openings that create a vivid sensory atmosphere or setting to draw the reader into the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, evocative description to establish mood and place; prioritize images and sensory detail that suggest larger stakes or themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical and thought-provoking
rubrics_metrics.description: A category of openings that present a statement, aphorism, or idea that frames the book's concerns or perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a striking thought or premise that signals the work's intellectual or thematic preoccupations and invites reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with the character’s voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Open using a distinct narrative or character voice so the reader immediately recognises who is speaking and their attitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the narrator/point-of-view's diction, perspective, or personality apparent in the first line to create immediacy and emotional connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start in the middle of something
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin in medias res — with action, conflict, or a moment of significance — rather than with exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drop the reader into a scene or event to create momentum; show an active situation that implies prior context and future consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a sense of mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft the opening so it withholds certain information, making readers want to learn more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce unanswered questions, unusual details, or partial information that compels readers to continue for clarification or payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it short and sharp
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer concise, tightly written first lines that deliver impact without excess words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for brevity and clarity; a short, well-phrased sentence often hooks better than a long, weighed-down one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clichés and aim for surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Steer clear of overused openings and familiar phrasing; instead, offer fresh imagery or an unexpected angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject predictable openings and seek originality — a surprising detail, twist of diction, or novel perspective will make the line memorable.
